finding_resolutions.explanation: Confirmed against GDD Section 2 (Loss and Floor-run restart ownership), which names 'encounter activation/admission state' as a required reset participant and requires every state owner to expose its own reset entry point. encounter-admission-cap-enforcement was the sole run-persistent owner in the candidate with no owner-side reset criterion while floor-run-restart-persistent-closure already depended on it. Because the parallel Evidence audit (EV-ENEM-003) appended a competing criterion to the same field, I merged both into one acceptance criterion and one validation requirement rather than adding near-duplicates: the CE floor-initial-state contract plus the evidence audit's concrete state enumeration (delayed/reduced pending activation, admitted-batch bookkeeping).

Confirmed: GDD line 23 ('Each room ends at a door'), line 25 (open the final door and escape), and line 50 ('The player moves through connected rooms toward the final door') require sealed-door connectivity and a designated final door, yet no work item obliged authoring door instances or designating the Final Room's exit — five-room-content-authoring covered only the five named spaces and single-scene continuity. Added the criterion to five-room-content-authoring because room connectivity is a room-geometry property, while dungeon-encounter-content-authoring's own scope ('configured per-door durability values') presupposes door instances already exist and the door items are reusable runtime components. The finding's human-review flag concerned only which deferred content feature hosts the criterion, which is a graph-representation choice within refiner authority; the requirement itself is explicitly specified, so no unresolved question was opened.

Confirmed: GDD Section 5 Runtime Implementation states Bone Archive's lane widths are validated against enemy movement/navigation requirements, and Section 4's Unity Validation Agent lists both 'Bone Archive lane pathing' and 'Chapel of Ash occlusion'. Both are joint checks over runtime configuration and authored geometry, but the candidate owned them only on enemy-pursuit-search-foundation, gameplay-navigation-locomotion, and ranged-enemy. Added the authoring-side halves as validation requirements on five-room-content-authoring so the geometry constraints survive future decomposition.

Confirmed in the GDD Dungeon Floor Structure table: Chapel of Ash contains 'the newly introduced Ranged Enemy, which appears here alongside Melee Enemy support rather than alone', while Ruined Entry and Bone Archive are described purely in melee terms. The pacing existed only as gdd_evidence prose, so the existing composition criteria would have permitted a Ranged Enemy in Ruined Entry. Added it as an obliging acceptance criterion on dungeon-encounter-content-authoring.

Verified the scope-cut paragraph verbatim in Section 5's Six-Week Development Plan, and confirmed no existing non_code_requirement covers it (the nearest, 'Agent scope and canon discipline', only forbids adding scope). Added a new typed pipeline_constraint, 'Schedule-slip scope-reduction order', preserving the ordered reduction policy and the protection of required systems. Classified as pipeline_constraint because it is a development-process invariant, not gameplay work.

Confirmed the Section 5 sentence 'encounter placement/content consumes the authored room spaces and the encounter-admission/cap foundation' verbatim. Restated the prerequisite in dungeon-encounter-content-authoring's decomposition_reason (a durable decomposition field rather than free-text notes), instructing a future Progressive Decomposer to attach the concrete descendant-to-descendant edge later. No feature-target dependency was introduced, so the dependency-kind invariant is preserved.

Confirmed encounter-admission-cap-enforcement is deliberately scoped to be dispatchable and testable without authored encounter content, so it cannot exercise per-encounter sizing. Removed the three-to-eight validation requirement from that item and added the matching validation requirement to dungeon-encounter-content-authoring, which owns the 3-8 acceptance criterion. The floor-wide fifteen-enemy ceiling remains validated on the admission item, so the Section 3 Player Experience Success Criterion stays represented on owning work items rather than being dropped.

Confirmed both quoted GDD sentences verbatim: Section 5 Runtime Implementation ('Character presentation is therefore part of the reusable visual-world foundation rather than a separate rendering architecture') and Section 3 Environment Presentation and Authoring Direction (wizard and enemy representations follow the same isometric sorting conventions). melee-enemy and ranged-enemy each claim delivery of an assembled SpriteRenderer archetype prefab conforming to conventions owned by world-visual-foundation, which is repository_state missing with no SpriteRenderer/Grid/Tilemap anywhere in Assets/. Added a depends_on edge from each archetype to world-visual-foundation (an implementation-kind target, no cycle introduced) rather than stripping the prefab-assembly criteria, since each archetype must retain an owner for usable prefab assembly.

Confirmed the GDD names enemy attack state as a reset participant distinctly from pursuit/search and status/displacement, and verified enemy-pursuit-search-foundation's reset criterion covers only target/last-known-position/search state. melee-enemy, ranged-enemy, and locked-door-enemy-attack carried no reset criteria and were absent from floor-run-restart-persistent-closure's participant list, leaving attack-state reset unowned. Added matching reset acceptance criteria and validation requirements to each owner and the three keys to the closure item's depends_on, mirroring the established pattern.

Confirmed the same gap CE-01 reports, from the evidence side: the item's three acceptance criteria covered only capacity querying, delay/reduce-first behavior, and non-duplication, while the closure item already assumed a reset interface. Because both audits wrote competing text to encounter-admission-cap-enforcement's acceptance_criteria and validation_requirements, I resolved the conflict by synthesizing a single criterion and single validation requirement that retain this finding's concrete state enumeration (pending delayed/reduced activation, admitted-batch bookkeeping) inside CE-01's floor-initial-state contract. No new dependency edge was needed.

Verified directly in the GDD: Section 2's Loss and Floor-run restart ownership paragraphs state registry bookkeeping resets to the floor's initial state and never say that state is empty, while each persistent enemy is returned to its authored spawn region in its initial AI state. 'Initial empty/starting state' was canon from silence and was replaced with the GDD's actual wording in both the acceptance criterion and validation requirement. Added a re-registration/consistency criterion so post-restart registry count cannot desynchronize from the live set of restored persistent enemies, worded neutrally so it does not assert whether the floor's initial active set is empty — which is deferred encounter-authoring content. No unresolved question was needed because the repair removes the unsupported assumption rather than replacing it with another.

result.reasoning:
Two audits (coverage_content_encounters and evidence_enemy_encounters) collided on encounter-admission-cap-enforcement's acceptance_criteria and validation_requirements: both appended a floor-restart reset criterion with different wording, and the coverage audit additionally removed the three-to-eight-enemy validation requirement from the same field. I verified the underlying requirement in the GDD (Section 2 Loss + Floor-run restart ownership both name "encounter activation/admission state" as a required reset participant and require owner-exposed reset entry points) and synthesized a single acceptance criterion and single validation requirement combining the coverage audit's floor-initial-state contract with the evidence audit's concrete state enumeration, avoiding duplicate near-identical criteria on one item.

All remaining operations from both proposals were independently verified against Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md and the frozen candidate before acceptance, with particular attention to quotation integrity: the Section 5 Six-Week Development Plan scope-cut paragraph, the Section 5 "Character presentation is therefore part of the reusable visual-world foundation" sentence, the Section 3 isometric-sorting sentence, the Section 5 "encounter placement/content consumes the authored room spaces" sentence, the Bone Archive lane-width validation sentence, the Section 4 Unity Validation Agent check list, and the Chapel of Ash "newly introduced Ranged Enemy" room description all exist verbatim in the cited locations. Nothing is attributed to CLAUDE.md, verification artifacts, or patch-round labels.

Structural closure re-checked: the two new archetype edges and three new closure edges all target implementation-kind items; no feature-target dependency was added (CE-06 was deliberately repaired via decomposition_reason instead of a dungeon-encounter -> five-room edge); no cycles are introduced since world-visual-foundation depends only on tilemap-navigation-package-configuration and the enemy/attack owners do not depend on floor-run-restart-persistent-closure; no exclusive_resources were changed, so no read-only consumer was serialized and no shared-writer key drifted. The Section 3 Player Experience Success Criterion for encounter sizing remains represented as a validation_requirement — relocated to the item that can exercise it, not deleted.

The one repair I softened rather than accepted verbatim is the registry re-registration criterion (EV-ENEM-004): the original phrasing asserted enemies re-register "as part of enemy-owned restart restoration", which edges toward specifying deferred authoring facts. I kept the bookkeeping-accuracy obligation and the normal activation-registration path, but removed language that would presume whether the floor's initial active set is empty or non-empty — the exact assumption the finding correctly identified as canon from silence.
